Status:
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx), Operating sheet, plant 55135, generator CT01, reads status '(OP) Operating', operating year 2000, no planned retirement year.
- The Wisconsin air permit 47115387A-P33 issued July 15, 2026 (https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1280163) lists this turbine as a simple cycle combustion turbine in the post-modification section.
- I found no retirement notice, mothballing or sale.

Capacity (MW).note:
Capacity:
- Alliant's Neenah page (https://www.alliantenergy.com/our-energy/natural-gas/neenah) says 'increasing capacity from roughly 300 to 440 megawatts' for both units, which is 220 MW each. This is the source Amalia Llano used, and her note carries it.
- The air permit 47115387A-P33 (https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1280163) lists each turbine as 'up to 218 MW'. This is close to 220 MW and supports the figure.
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 185.5 MW nameplate, 201 MW net summer and 218.9 MW net winter for CT01 and 200.1 and 218.4 for CT02. The nameplate is the old pre-upgrade value. I left 220 MW as it is.

units.notes: Still operating per EIA and the July 2026 permit. Backup Power: no document found that states it either way for this unit; the existing value no stays.

qa.question: Should Neenah units stay at 220 MW when EIA shows 185.5 MW nameplate?
qa.finding: Alliant's page at https://www.alliantenergy.com/our-energy/natural-gas/neenah says the 2025 upgrades raised the two turbines from about 300 to 440 MW, so 220 MW each. The air permit at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1280163 says up to 218 MW each. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) still shows the old 185.5 MW nameplate.
qa.recommendation: Leave 220 MW on both units. Recheck when EIA publishes its next annual survey.
qa.note: EIA net winter capacity is 218.9 MW for CT01 and 218.4 MW for CT02, which agrees with the permit.
